findings.text: Tauri's per-platform generated capability schemas are tracked in git, which guarantees perpetual unauthored churn on this repo's two-machine setup. `src-tauri/gen/schemas/` holds files Tauri regenerates on every build, one per platform; four are tracked (acl-manifests.json, capabilities.json, desktop-schema.json, macOS-schema.json) and have already churned across 1-3 commits each. The upstream Tauri 2 template ships a `src-tauri/.gitignore` containing `/gen/schemas`; this repo has no `src-tauri/.gitignore` at all, so that ignore was never adopted. Because a macOS host and a Linux VM share one mounted tree, each side's build rewrites or adds a schema the other side then sees as a dirty file it did not author -- currently `macOS-schema.json` is modified (+66 lines of `dialog:` plugin permissions, regenerated after the file-dialog plugin landed) and an untracked `linux-schema.json` (~117 KB) exists from a VM build. Recommendation: add `src-tauri/gen/schemas/` to .gitignore and `git rm --cached` the four tracked siblings in a separate housekeeping commit, so neither machine's build dirties the tree again. Untracking affects the other machine and any CI that reads these files, so it needs an explicit decision rather than being folded into an unrelated commit. If they are kept tracked instead, the modified macOS schema should be committed and linux-schema.json added, and the churn accepted as the cost.
